# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`), the tab progress bar (OSC 9;4, `terminalProgress`), the window title (`windowTitle`, restored by `internal/termtitle`), the terminal hand-off to child processes (the exec wrapper `internal/ui/teaexec`, use it instead of `tea.ExecProcess`, D121) and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci` (typed `StatusError`, `...Context` variants), `internal/imagesearch` and the registry browser's image search level, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface`, `internal/nettrace` (the path trace: unprivileged UDP + `IP_RECVERR` on Linux, ICMP echo through `iphlpapi` on native Windows) |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage`, `internal/ui/datatable`, and the activity indicator column (`internal/ui/indicator`, `datatable.IndicatorColumn`, the row sentences `components.DescribeRow`) |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# Planning Rules

## Implementation Plans

- **Location**: Always write implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` in the current project directory.
- **Format**: Use Markdown format for plans.
- **Naming**: Use descriptive names like `feature-name-plan.md` or `YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name.md`.

## Antigravity IDE Integration

When using the Antigravity IDE extension:
- Save all implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` relative to the project root.
- Create the directory if it doesn't exist before saving plans.
- Plans should be accessible from both Claude Code CLI and Antigravity IDE.

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected
- ✅ Document all quality changes

**Claude Code MUST NEVER:**
- ❌ Wait for the user to flag a warning
- ❌ Create a commit with unresolved warnings
- ❌ Ignore dependency issues
- ❌ Forget to update the documentation

### Correct workflow examples

**Example 1 - Feature commit:**
```
1. Write the code
2. go build → verify compilation
3. golangci-lint run → fix warnings
4. go test ./... → verify tests
5. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics → check the IDE
6. git commit with a detailed message
```

**Example 2 - Detecting a deprecated dependency:**
```
1. golangci-lint detects SA1019
2. Look up the recommended alternative
3. Replace the import and the code
4. go mod tidy
5. Test that everything works
6. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md
7. git commit explaining the replacement
```

### Rule 307 : Commits and code comments — English only

**Every git commit message and every comment in the code must be written
in English**, regardless of the language used to converse with the user.

| Element | Language |
|---------|--------|
| Commit message (title + body) | ✅ English only |
| Code comment (`//`, `/* */`, docstring) | ✅ English only |
| Replies to the user in the conversation | The user's language (see memory `feedback-langue-francais`) |
| UI and logs (Rule 129) | English US only — already covered, unchanged |

This **replaces** the earlier tolerance listed in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` under
"Code Conventions" ("Comments: French or English both accepted"): existing
French comments are not to be rewritten wholesale, but any new comment and
any edit to an existing comment must be in English.

```
// ✅ CORRECT
// retry with backoff because the API rate-limits bursts above 10 req/s

// ❌ WRONG (a French comment, which Rule 307 forbids)
// on relance avec un backoff car l'API limite les rafales au-delà de 10 req/s
```

```
✅ fix: correct table width calculation when a column is dropped

Bordures étaient soustraites deux fois, ce qui tronquait la dernière colonne.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

❌ fix: corrige le calcul de largeur de colonne
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ A commit message written in French, even partially
- ❌ A new code comment in French
- ❌ Confusing this rule with the language of the conversation, which
  remains the user's

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

3. **Sticky**: A -> B -> A (`/blob-back`) -> A's third request has no `Authorization`.
4. **Same-origin chain** (A -> A/other): Basic kept on each hop, entries returned.
5. **Downgrade (Q6)**: A `NewTLSServer`, blob 307 to `http://B/...` ->
   `errors.Is(err, errInsecureRedirect)`, B hits 0, no target path or query in the error.
   A https -> B https (both TLS) -> entries returned.
6. **Cap**: 11 hops between A and B -> `ErrTooManyRedirects`, no URL in the error.
7. **No signed URL in errors**: B hijacks and closes the connection -> error holds

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,

agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported

edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

  • oci.go:90 : le refus https vers http ne compare qu'à via[0]. Registre http, puis CDN https, puis http : l'URL signée repart en clair. Comparer plutôt au saut précédent (via[len(via)-1]).

input.message:
**Verdict : NON BLOQUANT** pour les étapes 3 (DEVDESK-517) et 4 (DEVDESK-518). Un point important (Referer) est à corriger avant la release.

**Exécuté sous plafond mémoire** : `go vet ./internal/oci` OK. `go test ./internal/oci ./internal/template -count=1` OK. `go test -race ./internal/oci -count=1` OK. `golangci-lint run ./internal/oci/...` : 0 issue. J'ai aussi lu les sources Go 1.27.4 (`net/http/client.go`, `archive/tar/reader.go`). Aucun fichier modifié. Commentaires Plane postés sur DEVDESK-518 et DEVDESK-517.

## Important
- **`/internal/oci/oci.go` ~79-98 (`followBlobRedirect`) : fuite du `Referer`.** `net/http` pose `Referer` = URL complète du saut précédent (`client.go:708`, via `refererForURL`), avant `CheckRedirect`. Sur une chaîne A (registre) → B (CDN) → C, C reçoit l'URL présignée de B (`sig=...`). L'exigence « URL signée ne sort pas » n'est donc pas tenue sur les chaînes à 2 hôtes ou plus. Pour A → B seul, B reçoit le chemin du blob du registre.
  - Correction : `req.Header.Del("Referer")` inconditionnel dans `followBlobRedirect`.
  - Ajouter un test à 3 hôtes qui vérifie l'absence de `Referer` sur C.

## Mineur
- **`oci.go` ~90 : le refus https → http ne compare qu'à `via[0]`.** Un registre http qui redirige vers un CDN https, lequel redirige vers http, renvoie l'URL signée en clair. Le plan et la décision Q6 disent `via[0]`, donc c'est conforme, mais comparer au saut précédent (`via[len(via)-1]`) serait plus sûr.
- **Commentaire de `blobCap` et plan : l'affirmation sur les répertoires est fausse.** Ils disent « une entrée répertoire avec une grosse taille est sautée sans être comptée ». Avec `archive/tar`, `isHeaderOnlyType` force la taille à 0 pour les répertoires.
  - Les octets réellement non comptés par `Limits` sont les en-têtes PAX/GNU, plus le bourrage.
  - Chaque en-tête est plafonné à 1 MiB par Go (`readSpecialFile`). Les en-têtes consécutifs remplacent `paxHdrs` au lieu de s'accumuler, donc pas de croissance mémoire.
  - Le plafond reste utile et le test 8 le valide. Il faut corriger le commentaire et le plan.
- **Tests manquants** :
  - un 3xx sans `Location` (il retombe sur l'erreur « failed to download layer: 302 », sans fuite) ;
  - un schéma non http(s) (`errBlobRedirectScheme`) ;
  - un appel direct de `followBlobRedirect`.

## Réponses point par point
1. **`followBlobRedirect` : conforme au plan.**
   - 10 sauts maximum, http/https seulement, https → http refusé (`errInsecureRedirect`).
   - `Authorization` supprimé si `req` ou un des `via[1:]` est hors origine de `via[0]` : suppression collante, jamais rétablie au retour sur l'origine. Le test 3 le couvre.
   - L'ordre est bon : `copyHeaders` s'exécute avant `checkRedirect`, donc la suppression dans `CheckRedirect` est ce qui part sur le réseau.
   - Le client ne pose que `Accept` et `Authorization`. Il n'y a pas de cookie jar ni de `Proxy-Authorization`, donc rien d'autre de sensible à copier.
   - Un 3xx sans `Location` renvoie la réponse telle quelle. Une redirection relative est résolue par `net/http` (test 4). Les 301/303 restent en GET, sans corps.
   - Seule fuite résiduelle : le `Referer`, ci-dessus.
2. **`sameOrigin`** compare le schéma et `Host` en chaîne exacte. « http://h » ≠ « http://h:80 » (et la casse compte aussi) : le coder a raison, c'est conservateur. Faux positif possible : refus côté manifest, `Authorization` supprimé côté blob. Jamais de fuite.
3. **`blobFetchError`** n'enveloppe que `ue.Err` (jamais le `*url.Error`) et n'ajoute que l'hôte. `StripRedirectTarget` est appliqué avant dans `get`. Aucune fuite de chemin ni de requête signée, test 7 compris.
4. **`cappedReader`** : pas d'off-by-one. Exactement `limit` octets passe, `limit+1` donne `ErrArchiveTooLarge`, qui traverse gzip et tar et reste joignable par `errors.Is`. Il n'y a pas de lecture illimitée : il lit au plus `limit` octets plus 1 octet de sonde.
   - **`blobCap` = 0 pour `Limits{}`** : acceptable. Le seul appelant de production (`internal/template/fetch.go:163-164`) fixe toujours `archiveLimits` (500 fichiers, 32 MiB), soit un plafond d'environ 34 MiB. Sans limites, rien ne borne la décompression non plus.
   - **Risque PAX géant** : faible. Mémoire bornée à 1 MiB par en-tête. Une bombe gzip d'en-têtes reste bornée en CPU par le timeout de 1 min et par le plafond de 34 MiB compressés. Le test 8 (3 × 500 KiB, sous la limite de 1 MiB de Go) est valide : sans plafond, le test « sans limites » lit bien l'archive.
5. **`TestBlobRedirectChainIsBounded`** : la modification est légitime et l'assertion n'est pas affaiblie.
   - `blobRegistry` enregistre déjà chaque requête de A dans `aHits`. Avec le `hop()` de A sur le même journal, chaque requête de A était comptée deux fois, donc « 10 requêtes » était insatisfiable.
   - Le compteur séparé `aHops` ne sert qu'à numéroter les sauts. L'assertion `aHits.count()-1 + bHits.count() == MaxRedirects` est inchangée et exacte (`len(via) >= 10` refuse la 11e requête). Je ne peux pas comparer à l'ancienne version, le fichier n'étant pas commité.
6. **Non-régression : OK.**
   - Manifest, `ListTags`, catalog, tags du registre et token gardent `RefuseOffOriginRedirect` (test 9 et `TestClientRefusesOffOriginRedirect`).
   - Le helper `get` pose Basic seulement si identifiant ET mot de passe sont renseignés.
   - Découpage 3/4 cohérent : le blob passe par `blobClient` dans l'état final. Je n'ai pas pu exécuter l'état intermédiaire de l'étape 3, qui n'est pas commité séparément. Le test de l'étape 3 ne fige pas le comportement du blob.
7. **Tests** :
   - Déterministes : serveurs `httptest` en `:0`, aucun port fermé ni réutilisé, transport `dialTo` pour les noms d'hôte.
   - Commentaires en anglais.
   - `-race` vert, et aucun programme ne lit un corps sans limite (fixture inférieure à 2 MiB).

## Observation hors diff
Le timeout de 1 min couvre aussi la lecture du corps (décision Q2). Un template d'environ 34 MiB sur une liaison lente expirerait avec une erreur peu parlante. Rien à faire ici.

## Recommandation sécurité
Le diff touche des identifiants et des redirections. Un passage par `security-reviewer` est recommandé. Le point à lui soumettre en priorité est le `Referer`.

Relecture du delta 412-4 (Referer, https vers http, SSRF, proxy) : verdict BLOQUANT sur un point (filtre SSRF contournable), le reste est non bloquant. go vet, golangci-lint (0 issue), go test ./internal/oci ./internal/template, go test -race ./internal/oci (aussi -count=3 sur Blob/Proxy/Dial) : verts.

Bloquant

  • oci.go isLocalAddr (~l.96) : l'adresse non spécifiée n'est pas filtrée. Vérifié avec un dialer dont Control copie la logique : http://0.0.0.0:PORT/ et http://[::]:PORT/ passent le filtre littéral et blobDialControl (« local=false »), et la connexion aboutit sur un service en 127.0.0.1 (Linux/macOS). Un registre public peut donc encore faire interroger un service local. Correction : || addr.IsUnspecified() dans isLocalAddr, avec des cas 0.0.0.0, [::], [::ffff:0.0.0.0] dans TestFollowBlobRedirectLocalTargets et TestBlobDialControl.

Important

  • oci.go NewClient (isLocalURL(registryURL)) : un registre dont le nom résout vers le loopback hors littéral/localhost est refusé par Control dès la requête du blob (le manifeste, lui, passe). Cas réel : k3d-registry.localhost:5000, ou une entrée /etc/hosts. Le message dit alors « refusing redirect » alors qu'aucune redirection n'a eu lieu. Corriger : traiter *.localhost comme local pour allowLocal, et trancher pour les alias /etc/hosts (documenter le refus ou autoriser l'adresse du registre).

Mineur

  • Message : le refus du dialer réutilise errBlobRedirectLocal (« refusing redirect to a loopback... »). Prévoir une erreur dédiée « refusing to connect to a loopback or link-local address » (le dialer) distincte du refus de redirection.
  • Derrière un proxy, seul le contrôle littéral de followBlobRedirect s'applique (le proxy résout la cible) : localhost., x.localhost et 0.0.0.0 passent. 127.1, 0x7f.1 et 2130706433 ne sont pas parsés par netip ni par le résolveur Go (dial échoue) ; Control reste de toute façon le filet sans proxy. Normaliser dans isLocalHost (point final, suffixe .localhost, IsUnspecified).
  • proxyAddrs.add : (1) un échec de résolution est mémorisé (seen=true) pour la vie du process, jamais réessayé ; (2) la résolution se fait hors verrou : une 2e requête concurrente voit seen=true avant le remplissage de addrs et se fait refuser un proxy local. Pas de data race (détecteur vert). La résolution bloque Proxy() jusqu'à 5 s sans contexte. Marquer seen après la résolution réussie, ou résoudre sous un singleflight.
  • Trou proxy : has() autorise l'ip:port du proxy y compris pour une connexion directe (NO_PROXY). Cela ne mène qu'au port du proxy lui-même, risque négligeable.
  • Lisibilité : oci.go passe à 566 lignes. Les ~250 lignes de garde et de transport (isLocal*, dialControl, proxyAddrs, blobTransport, followBlobRedirect, blobFetchError, blobCap, cappedReader) gagneraient à aller dans oci_blob.go (non imposé).

Points 1 (Referer supprimé hors origine) et 2 (https vers http comparé au saut précédent) : corrects et testés. Control s'applique à chaque dial (reconnexions, Happy Eyeballs, résolution DNS) et voit l'IP réellement composée : le rebinding est couvert. IPv4-mappé, zone IPv6 et fe80::/10 sont bien traités.

- `go test -race -run 'Blob|Proxy|Dial' -count=3` : vert.

- Le commentaire de revue est posté sur DEVDESK-518.

## Bloquant
- **`internal/oci/oci.go` ~l.96, `isLocalAddr` : l'adresse non spécifiée n'est pas filtrée.** La sonde montre que `0.0.0.0` et `::` donnent « control sees ... local=false » : `isLocalHost` les laisse passer et `blobDialControl` aussi. - **`oci.go`, `NewClient` (`isLocalURL(registryURL)`) : régression pour les registres dont le nom résout vers le loopback.**
  - Le blob passe par `blobClient`, dont le `Control` refuse le loopback ; le manifeste passe par `httpClient`, non gardé.

input.message:
**DEVDESK-519 (412-5, vérification du digest du blob) : NON BLOQUANT.** Aucun point bloquant ni important.

**Exécuté sous plafond mémoire :**
- `go vet ./internal/oci ./internal/template` : propre.
- `go test ./internal/oci ./internal/template -count=1` : vert.
- `go test -race ./internal/oci -count=1` : vert.
- `golangci-lint run ./internal/oci/... ./internal/template/...` : 0 issue.
- Aucun fichier modifié. Commentaire de revue posté sur DEVDESK-519.

## Réponses aux points demandés
1. **Ordre de lecture : correct.**
   - `io.TeeReader` enveloppe le flux compressé déjà plafonné (`cappedReader`), donc le hash couvre exactement les octets lus, read-ahead de gzip inclus.
   - `checkBlobDigest` draine le reste (octets après le flux gzip compris) puis compare le hash à la fin ; la comparaison n'est pas en temps constant, sans enjeu ici.
   - Un excès de plafond pendant le drain remonte en `ErrArchiveTooLarge`, pas en mismatch (testé).
   - Aucune entrée n'est retournée avant la fin de la vérification : `downloadAndExtractLayer` renvoie `nil` sur mismatch, `fetchOCI` (`internal/template/fetch.go`) ne manipule que de la mémoire, et `cache.go` n'écrit (fichier temporaire, `cache.go:235`) qu'après un `Fetch` réussi.
2. **Erreur de lecture gzip/tar et mismatch.**
   - Une erreur de lecture gzip/tar ou `ErrArchiveTooLarge` (limites) l'emporte sur le mismatch, parce que l'archive est analysée avant la fin du hachage. Rien n'est retourné : seul le diagnostic est moins précis.
   - Flux tronqué ou fin prématurée : le tar peut s'arrêter à une frontière sans lire le trailer gzip, mais le drain hache la suite, donc la troncature est détectée. Le digest couvre tout le flux ; c'est plus strict que le contrôle CRC de gzip.
3. **`parseLayerDigest` : strict.**

Checking whether the oci package pulls in anything from devdesk, which would create an import cycle; it doesn't appear to, and other packages already import it. I'm also looking at how the nexus error wraps the endpoint, and whether the host-building logic could leak credentials; since only the host is used and userinfo is excluded, it looks fine.

I'm checking the anonymous retry path: it fires on any error except an off-origin refusal, including too-large bodies and too-many-redirects, and since it sends no credentials it doesn't leak anything. I also note that the first authenticated request already went to the user's configured origin, so that part is fine. Last, I'm considering what happens if the group-members fetch is refused off-origin, since the log message would be misleading.

I'm weighing whether the sameOrigin check is too strict: it compares scheme and host, so an http://nexus redirect to https://nexus gets refused, even though that's a plain upgrade on the same host. That could break setups where a reverse proxy forces https, since the whole detection would fail. Allowing an http-to-https upgrade on the same hostname looks safer than refusing it, because the Basic credentials already went to that host.

I'm weighing whether to accept the http-to-https regression on the same host or add a narrow exception for it. The detection only breaks for users who explicitly type an http:// URL and whose server forces https, and the error already names the refused host, so I'm leaning toward documenting it as a minor note rather than changing the shared guard.

I'm checking the Nexus group-members size cap: a group's memberNames list is small, and even a repo's full metadata is only a few kilobytes, so 1 MiB is far above what a real response needs. The same-host http-to-https redirect regression applies to the other clients too, and a default-port variant like https://h versus https://h:443 is rare enough to ignore. The off-origin guard is also used for registry tags, which I'd already decided on.

I'm checking the Hub client next: it has no redirect handler, but the Hub is a fixed public endpoint and no credentials are sent to it, so that's fine. I also want to see how the calling code uses partial results when the metadata comes back empty on error, and whether the "response body over N bytes" error echoes any of the body, which I don't expect.

Next I'm checking where the Hub error surfaces and whether callers ever used partial metadata on failure, plus whether the Hub client sends any headers on redirects. After that I'll run a wider grep for other HTTP clients that read response bodies without a size limit.

Review 412-6 : verdict NON BLOQUANT. go vet, golangci-lint (0 issue), go test ./internal/registrymgr -count=2, go test ./internal/oci, go test -race ./internal/registrymgr : verts.

nexusHTTPClient refuse hors origine, nexusGET passe par StripRedirectTarget et ReadAllLimited. Aucun autre chemin HTTP de registre oublié : nexus.go n'a qu'un client ; imagesearch/hub.go borne déjà sa lecture ; les autres clients (status, netcheck) ne sont pas des clients de registre. Pas de cycle : internal/oci n'a aucune dépendance interne. La relance anonyme ne transporte aucun identifiant (anonInfo sans compte).

Important

  • nexus.go ~l.145 : après un refus de redirection hors origine, le log dit « account may lack nx-repository-admin privilege; run 'docker login' », ce qui est trompeur. Brancher sur errors.Is(err, oci.ErrOffOriginRedirect) : « members unreachable ... : redirect to another origin refused (the registry URL may need to be the one Nexus serves) », et réserver le conseil docker login aux HTTP 401/403 (le conseil s'affiche aujourd'hui pour toute erreur : délai, 404, trop gros).

Mineur

  • Impact d'une redirection http vers https du même hôte : sameOrigin compare schéma et hôte:port, donc http://nexus redirigé en https://nexus est refusé (régression pour une URL saisie en http:// avec un reverse proxy qui force https ; une URL sans schéma passe en https via parseNexusURL). Acceptable : l'erreur est explicite (hôte nommé) et se corrige en saisissant l'URL en https. Si le cas est fréquent, autoriser la montée http vers https de même nom d'hôte dans une garde sœur (les identifiants étaient déjà partis en clair vers cet hôte).
  • La relance anonyme part sur toute erreur sauf refus d'origine (délai, trop gros, trop de redirections) : sans fuite. La limiter à 401/403 demanderait une erreur typée à la place de fmt.Errorf("HTTP %d").
  • Plafond de 1 MiB non mesuré : risque de faux refus négligeable (soit environ 20 000 noms de membres) ; l'échec d'un endpoint de format trop gros est loggé et donne zéro membre.

Tests : déterministes, serveurs bornés à 3 MiB, verts sous -count=2 et -race.

**DEVDESK-520 (412-6, Nexus) : NON BLOQUANT, un point important sur le message de log. DEVDESK-521 (412-7, Hub) : NON BLOQUANT, rien d'important.**

**Exécuté sous plafond mémoire :**
- `go vet` sur `./internal/registrymgr`, `./internal/ui/oci_resources` et `./internal/oci` : propre.
- `go test ./internal/registrymgr -count=2` : vert.
- `go test ./internal/ui/oci_resources ./internal/oci -count=1` : vert.
- `go test -race ./internal/registrymgr ./internal/ui/oci_resources -count=1` : vert.
- `golangci-lint` sur `registrymgr` et `ui/oci_resources` : 0 issue.
- Aucun fichier modifié. Commentaires de revue postés sur DEVDESK-520 et DEVDESK-521.

## DEVDESK-520 (Nexus)

### Important
- **`internal/registrymgr/nexus.go` ~l.145 (`fetchGroupMembers`)** : après un refus de redirection hors origine, le log dit « account may lack nx-repository-admin privilege; run 'docker login' with an admin account ». C'est trompeur.
  - Correction : brancher sur `errors.Is(err, oci.ErrOffOriginRedirect)` pour écrire « redirect to another origin refused (the registry URL may need to be the one Nexus serves) ».
  - Réserver le conseil `docker login` aux HTTP 401/403 : il s'affiche aujourd'hui pour toute erreur (délai, 404, réponse trop grosse).
  - Le test 2 vérifie seulement que le log contient la phrase du refus, donc il resterait vert.

### Mineur
- **Redirection http → https du même hôte (point 2)** : `sameOrigin` compare schéma et hôte:port, donc `http://nexus` redirigé vers `https://nexus` est refusé.
  - C'est une vraie régression, limitée aux URL saisies avec `http://` derrière un reverse proxy qui force https (une URL sans schéma passe en https via `parseNexusURL`).
  - Acceptable : l'erreur est explicite (hôte nommé) et se corrige en saisissant l'URL en https.
  - Si le cas est fréquent, une garde sœur autorisant la montée http → https du même nom d'hôte serait sûre, puisque Basic était déjà parti en clair vers cet hôte.
- **Relance anonyme (point 3)** : elle part sur toute erreur sauf `ErrOffOriginRedirect` (délai, 404, réponse trop grosse, trop de redirections). Elle ne fuit rien : `anonInfo` est sans identifiant. La limiter à 401/403 demanderait une erreur typée à la place de `fmt.Errorf("HTTP %d")`.
- **Plafond 1 MiB non mesuré (point 4)** : risque de faux refus négligeable (environ 20 000 noms de membres). Un endpoint de format trop gros est loggé et donne zéro membre.

### Points validés
- **Chemins HTTP (point 1)** : `nexus.go` n'a qu'un client et un seul chemin (`nexusGET`), couvert. `imagesearch/hub.go` borne déjà sa lecture. `status/http_checker.go` et `netcheck/env.go` ne sont pas des clients de registre. Aucun `io.ReadAll` non borné en production hors de `internal/oci/oci.go:274`, qui est déjà sous `LimitReader`.
- **Cycle (point 6)** : aucun. `internal/oci` n'a aucune dépendance interne. Le couplage `registrymgr` → `oci` se limite à la garde de redirection et à `ReadAllLimited`.
- **Tests (point 7)** : déterministes, serveurs bornés à 3 MiB, verts sous `-count=2` et `-race`.

## DEVDESK-521 (Hub)
- `fetchDockerHubTagsMeta` lit via `oci.ReadAllLimited` avec un plafond de 4 MiB, soit environ 7,9 fois la plus grosse page citée dans le commentaire (530629 octets). Je n'ai pas revérifié cette mesure, faute d'accès réseau.
- Erreur « hub API: %w » enveloppant `ErrBodyTooLarge`, `meta` nil, aucun écho du corps ni résultat partiel (`commands.go:419-421`). `handleMultiRegistryTagsMeta` ignore la méta et logge l'erreur.
- Le commentaire de la fonction est corrigé : plus de « partial results ».
- Le client Hub n'envoie aucun identifiant, donc l'absence de garde de redirection ne peut pas faire fuiter de secret.
- **Mineur** : dans `hub_tags_meta_bound_test.go`, le faux Hub peut servir jusqu'à 8 MiB avant d'échouer, mais le test borne les octets réellement lus (plafond + 1) et n'alloue rien. Sans conséquence.

## Rappel
Le point bloquant de ma relecture de DEVDESK-518 (`isLocalAddr` sans `IsUnspecified`, donc `0.0.0.0` et `[::]` non filtrés) n'est pas revérifié ici.

{"result":{"id":"26813bc2-edfa-40b2-bd6b-931715b8291b","assignees":[],"labels":["0d75b934-bc35-4b5d-9e3b-362237efc0a6"],"type_id":null,"created_at":"2026-11-14T08:33:49.584958Z","updated_at":"2026-11-16T16:11:17.620219Z","deleted_at":null,"point":null,"name":"Registry HTTP clients: extend the origin and size hardening of DEVDESK-410 to the other clients","description_html":"

Story

As a DevDesk user who configures registries (OCI, Nexus) and a hostile or misconfigured server could answer them, I want every HTTP client that talks to a registry to refuse a redirect or a Bearer realm that would send my credentials elsewhere or in clear, to bound what it reads, and to keep credentials out of error messages, so that the hardening of DEVDESK-410 (limited to internal/oci's registry client) also covers the other clients.

Acceptance criteria

  • Given the http.Client of internal/oci/oci.go (line 46, no CheckRedirect, no timeout; Basic auth sent at lines 60, 96 and 148), when a registry answers a redirect outside the origin of the first request, then the redirect is refused with the same error as DEVDESK-410 (refuseOffOriginRedirect, host only, no path or query) and no credentials are sent to the target.

  • Given that same client, when a server does not answer, then the call ends after a bounded timeout instead of hanging.

  • Given the Nexus client (internal/registrymgr/nexus.go, line 28 and lines 201-212; Basic auth, redirects followed, unbounded io.ReadAll), when Nexus answers a redirect outside the origin, then it is refused and no credentials are sent to the target.

  • Given that Nexus client, when a response body exceeds the cap, then an error is returned (no silent cut) and memory stays bounded.

  • Given the Docker Hub calls of internal/ui/oci_resources/commands.go (lines 362 and 412, fixed host hub.docker.com, no credentials, low severity), when a response body exceeds the cap, then an error is returned and memory stays bounded.

  • Given an https registry that announces a Bearer realm in http:// (medium severity: the Basic credentials are sent in clear to the token endpoint), when a token is requested, then the realm is refused with an error, and no request is sent to it.

  • Given an apiURL that contains a userinfo (REDACTED), when a request fails, then the error prefix built by internal/oci/registry.go shows the URL through url.Redacted() and the REDACTEDword appears neither in the footer nor in the logs.

  • Given a registry that redirects in a loop on the same origin, when the 10-redirect limit is reached, then the error \"stopped after 10 redirects\" no longer carries the raw URL (it is masked like the other redirect errors; low severity).

  • Given same-origin links and redirects that DEVDESK-410 already allows, when any of these clients runs, then behaviour is unchanged and existing tests stay green.

Context

Effort: M (to be validated by the architect). Priority: medium, driven by the Bearer realm in http:// (point 4, medium severity); the other points are low severity.

Dependency: this story depends on the merge of DEVDESK-410 (PR in progress), which introduces refuseOffOriginRedirect, sameOrigin, errOffOriginRedirect and the 1 MiB token cap (maxTokenResponse). Do not start before it is merged.

Source: decision D142 in docs/backlog.md (worktree .worktrees/fix/devdesk-410-registry-credential-origin, not yet merged), which lists these as \"found and not fixed, out of scope\", plus two residual risks (Bearer realm in http://, raw URL in the error prefix of registry.go). Scope in six points: (1) internal/oci/oci.go:46: reuse refuseOffOriginRedirect and add a timeout; (2) internal/registrymgr/nexus.go:28 and 201-212: origin refusal and bounded read; (3) internal/ui/oci_resources/commands.go:362 and 412: bounded read; (4) refuse a Bearer realm in http:// announced by an https registry; (5) url.Redacted() in the error prefix of registry.go; (6) mask the \"stopped after 10 redirects\" error. Tests: httptest with two servers, as in internal/oci/catalog_test.go (TestListCatalogContextNextOrigin).

Out of scope

  • Changing DEVDESK-410 or its fixes (tags next, registryHTTPClient, token cap).

  • Supporting registries that legitimately redirect to another host (CDN or object storage): the explicit refusal of D142 stays.

  • A silent anonymous retry after a refused redirect.

  • Changes to credential storage (internal/credentials) or to the image-signature checks.

  • New configuration options (timeout or cap set by the user).

Rule for tests that follows: never serve or read an endless body without a cap; bound it with a sentinel error (a reader that fails after N bytes, a handler that stops on the first write error), never rely on the timeout. D145 rejected it as stale and as possibly routing several addresses where the trace uses the first. Here the reading is kept with the results on screen and discarded with them, so it is never stale beyond that (key: host, address, source), and the trace prefers an address Diagnostics already read with success (point 5), so the two no longer disagree. Why: one routing-table read per address and one answer on screen, also on round-robin names. Decided (user, 2026-11-15): (1) On windows/amd64 (and the other Windows architectures once measured), `internal/nettrace` runs one `IcmpSendEcho2` call (`iphlpapi.dll`, synchronous) per TTL, each in its own goroutine, as D143 does for its sockets. The call takes no admin rights: it is what `tracert.exe` uses. The Linux design of D143 (UDP to port 33435, `IP_RECVERR`) is unchanged. (2) "Reached" on Windows means an Echo Reply from the target, not a Port Unreachable. A router's Time Exceeded ends nothing; a Destination Unreachable from a router still ends the trace as `HopUnreachable`, as on Linux. Linux's stricter source check is not mirrored. (5) Windows Firewall: Time Exceeded and Echo Reply to our outgoing echoes pass without any rule and without admin, as with `tracert`. A third-party firewall can make hops silent; that is not detected. Measured on Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300 (dev machine), amd64: a live trace to `1.1.1.1` reached the target in 15 hops; TTL 1, 2 and 8 answered as routers, the other intermediate hops stayed silent, and no firewall error appeared. windows/arm64 and 386 are not measured; the struct layout is pinned by `TestEchoReplyLayout`. Why: no admin, the same mechanism as `tracert`, and error codes that do not depend on the Windows language. **Revue finale DEVDESK-412 : NON BLOQUANT.** Un point important, côté documentation uniquement. Aucun point bloquant de code.

**Exécuté sous plafond mémoire :**
- `go vet` des 4 paquets (`oci`, `registrymgr`, `template`, `ui/oci_resources`) : propre.
- `go test` des 4 paquets `-count=1` : vert.
- `go test -race ./internal/oci ./internal/registrymgr` : vert.
- `golangci-lint` sur les 4 paquets : 0 issue ; `gofmt -l` : rien.
- Aucun fichier modifié. Commentaire de revue posté sur DEVDESK-412.

**Corrections des passes précédentes, vérifiées dans le code :**
- `isLocalAddr` et `isLocalHost` filtrent maintenant `0.0.0.0`, `[::]`, `*.localhost` et `localhost.` (`internal/oci/oci_blob.go`).
- Le refus au dial a sa propre erreur : `errBlobDialLocal`.
- Le log Nexus après refus d'origine ne donne plus le conseil `docker login` (`internal/registrymgr/nexus.go`).
- `errBlobDigestForm` dit « unsupported layer digest: only sha256 is supported ».
- `proxyAddrs` est sérialisé et un échec de résolution n'est plus mémorisé.
- `Referer` supprimé hors origine.

## Important (documentation)
- **`docs/architecture/network.md`, bloc « URLs are redacted »** : il écrit que `browser_bridge.go` journalise `oci.RedactURL(msg.RegistryURL)`. Le code appelle `oci.RedactRegistryURL` (`internal/oci/guard.go:62`).
  - Cette fonction n'est citée ni dans `network.md` ni dans la liste des exports de D156 (`docs/backlog.md`).
  - Ne sont pas non plus documentés : les logs de `registries.go` et `commands.go` (login/logout) et `redactGitURL` (`internal/template/fetch.go`).
  - Corriger le nom et compléter ces passages.

## Mineur
- **`redactGitURL` et `oci.RedactURL`** : `url.Redacted()` ne masque que le mot de passe.
  - Un jeton placé en nom d'utilisateur (`https://TOKEN@github.com/org/repo.git`, forme courante) reste affiché dans « fetching ... ».
  - Proposition : masquer aussi le nom d'utilisateur seul pour http(s), pas pour `ssh://git@...`.
  - Les formes demandées sont couvertes : `REDACTED` et `REDACTED` sont masquées (comportement de `url.Parse` / `Redacted`). La forme scp (`git@host:path`) est laissée telle quelle sans perte d'information utile (elle n'a ni schéma ni mot de passe). Les tests de `internal/template` passent.
  - `validateGitURL` refuse `file://`, donc pas de « `<invalid URL>` » sur ce chemin.
  - La dernière ligne de stderr de git est reprise dans le message ; git anonymise en général l'URL dans ses messages d'accès.
- **`internal/template/fetch_test.go`** : le test `TestFetchGitErrorNamesTheSourceWithoutItsPassword` ne couvre que `REDACTED`. Ajouter `REDACTED` et la forme scp inchangée.
- **AC2, `internal/oci/oci_client_origin_test.go:167`** : `TestNewClientIsBounded` ne vérifie que `httpClient.Timeout`, pas `blobClient.Timeout`. Il n'y a pas non plus de test de blocage réel.
- **`docs-site/docs/how-to/create-a-repo-from-a-template.md`** : « Errors name the host only, never the full address » est trop fort. Les erreurs du manifeste et des tags gardent l'URL (chemin du registre, mot de passe masqué). Écrire plutôt « never a password or a signed query ».
- **`docs/architecture/registries.md`** : un endpoint de format Nexus trop gros ou en échec (hors refus d'origine) donne toujours le conseil « account may lack nx-repository-admin privilege » dans le log. Le texte « ends the discovery the same way » est approximatif.
- **`internal/oci/registry.go`, `exchangeBearerTokenContext`** : 63 lignes, au-dessus du seuil de 50 de `.claude/rules/code-editing.md`. À scinder si l'occasion se présente.
- **Cohérence doc/code (point 3), le reste est exact** : plafonds 1 MiB Nexus, 4 MiB Hub (530629 octets mesurés) et `blobCap = Bytes + Files*2048 + 1 MiB` ; timeout d'1 min ; liste de refus SSRF (`localhost`, `*.localhost`, loopback, link-local, `0.0.0.0`) ; noms `StripRedirectTarget`, `errInsecureTokenRealm`, `checkTokenRealm`, `blobFetchError`, `checkBlobDigest` ; `D156` y compris les risques résiduels. Commentaires et messages en anglais (Rule 129).

## Table AC → test (story DEVDESK-412)
| AC | Test(s) |
|---|---|
| AC1 (modifié Q1b) | Refus tags/manifeste : `TestClientRefusesOffOriginRedirect`, `TestOtherCallsStillRefuseOffOriginRedirect`. Blob suivi sans identifiants : `TestBlobRedirectOffOriginDropsCredentials`, `TestBlobRedirectToSubdomainDropsCredentials`, `TestBlobRedirectCredentialsStayDroppedWhenChainReturns`, `TestBlobRedirectChainSendsNoReferer`, `TestBlobRedirectDowngrade*`, `TestFollowBlobRedirectLocalTargets`, `TestBlobDialControl`, `TestBlobRedirectToLocalTargetIsRefusedEndToEnd`. |
| AC2 | `TestNewClientIsBounded` (httpClient seul ; blobClient non couvert, pas de test de blocage réel). |
| AC3 | `TestNexusMetaRedirectOffOriginIsRefused`, `TestNexusFormatEndpointRedirectOffOriginIsRefused`, `TestNexusAnonymousRetryDoesNotFollowAnOffOriginRedirect`. |
| AC4 | `TestNexusResponseOverTheCapIsAnError`. |
| AC5 | `TestHubTagsMetaReadIsBounded`. |
| AC6 | `TestInsecureBearerRealmRefusedBeforeAnyRequest`, `TestNonHTTPBearerRealmRefused`, `TestCheckTokenRealm`, `TestExchangeBearerTokenRefusesAnInsecureRealmItself`. |
| AC7 | `TestRegistryErrorPrefixHidesThePassword*`, `TestRegistryRetryPrefixHidesThePassword`, `TestRegistryBuildRequestErrorHidesThePassword`, `TestBrowserBridgeLogsDoNotCarryTheRegistryPassword`, `TestRegistryTabLogsDoNotCarryThePassword`, `TestRedactURL`, `TestRedactRegistryURL`, `TestNexusUnreadableURLIsLoggedWithoutTheURL`, `TestFetchGitErrorNamesTheSourceWithoutItsPassword`. |
| AC8 | `TestRegistryRedirectLimitCarriesNoTarget`, `TestBlobRedirectChainIsBounded`. |
| AC9 | `TestClientFollowsSameOriginRedirect`, `TestNexusSameOriginRedirectIsFollowedWithCredentials`, `TestBlobRedirectSameOriginChainKeepsCredentials` ; tests existants verts. |

Aucun AC « non couvert », mais AC2 ne couvre pas `blobClient.Timeout`.
